mainTopic: Does רבי hold of מוקצה? Resolving the contradiction about בהמות מדבריות, and the closing of מסכת ביצה
overview: In a ברייתא, רבי ruled that true בהמות מדבריות (desert animals that never come into town) are מוקצה and may not be slaughtered on יום טוב. The גמרא challenged this. רבי once told his son that רבי שמעון holds מוקצה only for גרוגרות וצימוקין (figs and grapes set out to dry), which suggests desert animals should be permitted. The עמוד opens with the last words of that challenge. Then the גמרא gives three answers, each starting with איבעית אימא. First, desert animals are like drying figs and raisins, because the owner actively sent them away. Second, רבי was only reporting רבי שמעון's view and does not hold it himself. Third, רבי really holds there is no מוקצה, and in the ברייתא he was arguing with the רבנן on their own terms, but they rejected his argument. The עמוד ends with the הדרן, closing פרק משילין פירות and the whole מסכת ביצה.

steps.title: The challenge ends: only dried figs and raisins are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the challenge: according to רבי שמעון, as quoted by רבי, nothing is מוקצה except גרוגרות וצימוקין, so desert animals should not be מוקצה either.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a question that started on the previous עמוד. רבי had said that for רבי שמעון the only מוקצה is figs and raisins set out to dry, so how can רבי call desert animals מוקצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs and raisins are special. They were edible, and the owner pushed them out of his mind by setting them aside to dry, which makes them inedible for a while. Desert animals were never actively pushed away, so if only figs and raisins count, desert animals should be permitted. That clashes with רבי's ruling in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried figs, here figs spread out to dry
Raisins, here grapes spread out to dry
Only, alone
Set aside from use, so it may not be used on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This עמוד starts in the middle of the challenge. The words 'except dried figs and raisins alone' are the end of רבי's statement that the גמרא quoted as a contradiction. They are not a new ruling.

phrases.english: except dried figs and raisins alone!
phrases.notes: End of the quoted statement used to challenge רבי

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling in the ברייתא that true desert animals are מוקצה on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מוקצה applies only to items the owner actively pushed out of mind (figs and raisins drying), desert animals, which were never actively pushed away, should not be מוקצה.

steps.title: First answer: desert animals are like drying figs and raisins
steps.stepSummary: Desert animals belong in the same group as figs and raisins, because the owner actively sent them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: these animals are also like dried figs and raisins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. Desert animals are treated just like the figs and raisins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner sent the animals far away to graze, and they never come back into town. That is an active pushing away, like setting fruit out to dry. So even רבי שמעון's narrow view of מוקצה would include them, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say; introduces one of several possible answers
These too
Are similar to, are comparable

phrases.english: these too are like dried figs and raisins,
phrases.notes: Desert animals were actively sent away by the owner

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָנֵי נָמֵי כִּגְרוֹגְרוֹת וְצִמּוּקִין דָּמֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-categorization: the case fits inside the narrow exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Desert animals are different from figs and raisins, so they should not be מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: Desert animals were actively removed from the owner's mind, just like drying fruit, so they are מוקצה even for רבי שמעון

steps.title: Second answer: רבי was only reporting רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: When רבי told his son that רבי שמעון holds מוקצה only for figs and raisins, he was describing רבי שמעון's opinion, not his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: he said it according to the words of רבי שמעון, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבי was only explaining someone else's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction depended on assuming that רבי agreed with what he said in the name of רבי שמעון. If he was only reporting it, רבי himself can hold a broader view of מוקצה. Then his ruling that desert animals are מוקצה is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his words, as he holds
He was saying
He does not hold that way

phrases.english: he spoke according to the words of Rabbi Shimon,
but he himself does not hold this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement reports another person's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי agreed with the narrow view of מוקצה he quoted
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי only reported רבי שמעון's view and holds a broader view of מוקצה himself

steps.title: Third answer: רבי argued using the רבנן's own view
steps.stepSummary: רבי himself does not hold of מוקצה. In the ברייתא he was arguing with the רבנן on their own terms: even if you hold of מוקצה, agree that animals who come home at the first rain are domestic.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: he was speaking to the רבנן according to their view. 'For me, there is no מוקצה. But for you: at least agree with me that animals which go out to graze at פסח and come back at the first rainfall are domestic animals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. רבי really agrees with רבי שמעון that there is no מוקצה, and in the ברייתא he was only arguing from the רבנן's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer reverses the second answer. Here רבי truly holds there is no מוקצה, so the contradiction is solved from the other side. His words in the ברייתא were a 'even according to you' argument. He wanted the רבנן to at least move animals that come home for the winter into the 'domestic' category.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their words, using their position
According to me
According to you (plural)
At least agree with me
The first rainfall of the season (in חשון)
Domestic animals that live in or near town

steps.confusionAlert: The second and third answers are opposites. In the second, רבי holds of מוקצה and was only reporting רבי שמעון. In the third, רבי does not hold of מוקצה and was only arguing from the רבנן's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא solves a contradiction. A sage may argue 'even according to you' without accepting the other side's basic position.

phrases.english: he spoke to them according to the words of the Rabbis.
According to me, there is no muktze,
where they go out and graze from Passover
and come in at the first rainfall

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same challenge, the reverse of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument from the other side's view: the statement in the ברייתא was made for the sake of argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's words in the ברייתא show that he himself holds of מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי holds there is no מוקצה and was only trying to narrow the רבנן's view on their own terms

steps.title: The רבנן reject רבי's argument
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answered רבי: no, animals that graze outside from פסח until the first rain are still desert animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן said to him: No, they are desert animals.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the third answer's reading of the ברייתא. The רבנן did not accept רבי's 'at least agree with me' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the ברייתא is a debate. רבי tried to get the רבנן to call seasonal grazers domestic, and they refused. Since they stay outside for most of the year, the רבנן still call them מדבריות, and so they are מוקצה on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Desert animals that graze far from town and are treated as מוקצה
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers for why רבי calls desert animals מוקצה. (1) They are like drying figs and raisins. (2) רבי was only reporting רבי שמעון's view. (3) רבי was arguing on the רבנן's terms, and they rejected his argument.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis said to him:

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: לָא, מִדְבָּרִיּוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the third answer by giving the רבנן's reply to רבי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי's suggestion that animals coming home at the first rain count as domestic
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The animals spend most of the year outside town, so the רבנן still treat them as desert animals

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק משילין פירות and מסכת ביצה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the fifth פרק, משילין פירות, and for the whole מסכת ביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, משילין פירות, and מסכת ביצה is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional הדרן line. It marks the end of the פרק and the end of the מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no legal content here. The line declares that the learner will return to this פרק, and it marks the completion of מסכת ביצה, a time for a סיום.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing formula of a פרק
It is completed, finished
Tractate

phrases.english: We will return to you, Mashilin Peirot,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final sugya
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The end of פרק משילין פירות and of מסכת ביצה
